learningObjective: Use partial partition only to select top-k membership, then sort those candidate indices by their scores for the required descending order.

mechanismReview.pattern: Partial top-k membership selection followed by sorting only the selected subset.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: Use argpartition when k ranked elements are needed from a much larger score vector and fully sorting all n scores is unnecessary.
mechanismReview.invariant: After partition, every selected candidate belongs to the top-k score group although candidate order is unspecified; after subset argsort reversal, those same indices are descending by score.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Retain the score vector, valid k, k candidate indices, their gathered scores, and the permutation that orders only those candidates.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: Stable candidate identities move from their original score positions into the gathered subset and final index output, while labels explicitly separate unordered membership from descending order.
rejectedAlternatives: Sorting all scores is simpler but changes the supplied O(n + k log k) mechanism to O(n log n).
A heap can maintain top k but does not match the vectorized argpartition implementation.
Calling partition output already sorted is incorrect because argpartition guarantees membership, not candidate order.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Separate selection from ordering: first isolate the small set that can contain the answer, then pay sorting cost only on that set.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.
